doctrine.admission_rule: A pylon is admitted only when the same causal transaction appears in at least two distinct ecosystem categories, names its authority boundary, identifies its forbidden collapse, and yields a concrete proof transaction.
doctrine.control_question: Which causal structures recur across otherwise unrelated compute ecosystems, and what invariant surface should ahead-rev-sim preserve so every implementation can be consumed as a replaceable commodity?
doctrine.shape_definition: A congruent shape is a scale-independent causal structure, rather than a visual resemblance or shared vocabulary. It identifies where agency, state, authority, evidence, and cost move through a system.
doctrine.statement: The pylon catalog converts recurring ecosystem structures into design constraints. A pylon guides interfaces, receipts, tests, and succession without granting any witness project architectural authority.

pylons.authority_location: The accepted-work contract and hidden verifier remain outside every worker, provider, device, facility, and compiler.
design_consequences: Freeze the starting state and task identity before execution.
Represent each candidate as a bounded transition rather than mutable ambient state.
Seal candidate output, verifier result, replay material, and first divergence together.
Compare implementations only after replaying from the same frozen base.
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse execution completion into accepted work, or a provider response into repository state.
pylons.invariant: Frozen base plus bounded task packet plus replaceable worker produces a candidate transition that is verified, receipted, replayed, and compared outside the worker.
pylons.name: Bounded transition spine
pylons.proof_transaction: Replay one candidate from a frozen base, reproduce the accepted result and receipt, then identify the first divergence after intentional tampering.
pylons.shape_notation: frozen base + bounded packet + replaceable worker -> candidate delta -> verifier -> receipt -> replay -> comparison

pylons.authority_location: The programme owns workload identity, acceptance, fallback, evidence, publication, and succession. The provider owns only its declared implementation surface.
design_consequences: Keep acceptance and publication APIs inaccessible to providers.
Require provider replacement without changing workload or receipts.
Represent offers, submissions, acknowledgements, and qualification as distinct states.
Treat public announcements as intake signals rather than implementation evidence.
failure_modes: fallback controlled by the accelerated implementation
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not merge the actor performing work with the authority accepting, publishing, or preserving it.
pylons.invariant: Execution authority is narrower than acceptance authority, and both remain narrower than architectural and historical custody.
pylons.name: Authority outside provider
pylons.proof_transaction: Replace a named provider with a reference implementation while preserving the accepted result, refusal behavior, fallback, evidence boundary, and historical receipt chain.
pylons.shape_notation: provider executes inside declared surface; acceptance, fallback, evidence, and publication remain outside

pylons.authority_location: The verifier and receipt layer define refusal, fault, absence, uncertainty, and unresolved boundaries before any positive claim is admitted.
design_consequences: Give refused, faulted, missing, and not-applicable outcomes stable identities.
Retain blockers in the same artifact as successful observations.
Require ambiguous command or evidence states to fail closed.
Use missing evidence to generate the next transaction rather than prose optimism.
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse missing, refused, faulted, unmeasured, simulated, and accepted states into one boolean success field.
pylons.invariant: Negative space is executable evidence. The system must preserve why a claim was refused and what transaction would remove the blocker.
pylons.name: Negative-space refusal ledger
pylons.proof_transaction: Submit ambiguous, incomplete, stale, and faulting fixtures and prove that each produces a distinct terminal receipt without mutating accepted state.
pylons.shape_notation: candidate -> accepted | refused | faulted | unmeasured, each with immutable blockers and next transaction

pylons.authority_location: The estate retains the source-to-build-to-execution-to-measurement-to-supersession chain independently of any current maintainer or facility.
design_consequences: Hash every authority-changing artifact and transformation.
Bind source, tool, model, PDK, firmware, calibration, execution, and measurement identities.
Record supersession without deleting prior accepted evidence.
Require artifact-only reconstruction by an external acceptor.
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not replace historical custody with a link to the current vendor, branch, facility, or documentation page.
pylons.invariant: Every accepted transition remains reconstructable after its original actor, tool, facility, or programme disappears.
pylons.name: Provenance and succession chain
pylons.proof_transaction: Reconstruct one accepted result from pinned artifacts after removing the original builder, network service, and current documentation from the path.
pylons.shape_notation: source -> model/build -> execution -> measurement -> acceptance -> supersession, each edge signed and replayable

pylons.authority_location: The cartridge descriptor declares capabilities and lifecycle; the workload and acceptance layers remain external.
design_consequences: Require stable identity, capabilities, commands, state, reset, and receipt endpoints.
Use opaque handles rather than provider-owned address semantics.
Keep a software fallback behind the same accepted-work contract.
Make optional acceleration unable to alter evidence or semantics.
failure_modes: raw pointer authority crossing the boundary
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse a substrate, package, protocol, and workload into one proprietary execution island.
pylons.invariant: A heterogeneous implementation is consumable through identity, descriptor, capability, lifecycle, state, fallback, and receipt surfaces that survive provider replacement.
pylons.name: Self-describing cartridge
pylons.proof_transaction: Swap two implementations behind one descriptor and command lifecycle, then reproduce admission, refusal, reset, output, and receipt behavior.
pylons.shape_notation: identity + descriptor + capabilities + lifecycle + state + fallback + receipt = replaceable cartridge

pylons.authority_location: The accepted workload and comparison harness own equivalence; the physical implementation and reference twin are peers under that authority.
design_consequences: Require a public reference twin for every physical implementation class.
Use identical workload identity and accepted-output rules on both paths.
Record first model-to-hardware divergence rather than averaging it away.
Keep fallback executable after hardware admission.
failure_modes: model calibrated on held-out test data
physical claim inferred from model agreement
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse a model, simulator, emulator, and measured device into one undifferentiated evidence tier.
pylons.invariant: Every physical candidate competes against a pinned reference twin under the same accepted work while preserving where and why their trajectories diverge.
pylons.name: Reference-twin substitution
pylons.proof_transaction: Run one immutable workload through the physical candidate and reference twin, compare accepted output and first divergence, then remove the physical path and replay the receipt through fallback.
pylons.shape_notation: physical candidate || reference twin, joined only by fixed workload, acceptance, and divergence receipt

pylons.authority_location: The lifecycle state machine owns legal transitions and terminal outcomes; providers implement transitions but cannot invent terminal meaning.
design_consequences: Declare discovery, configure, load, run, read, capture, reset, refuse, and fault states.
Make commands one-hot or transactionally serialized.
Keep control state immutable while busy.
Require reset and refusal receipts before admitting useful work.
failure_modes: remote queue completion mistaken for task success
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse transport completion, device completion, task acceptance, refusal, and fault into one status bit.
pylons.invariant: Every replaceable component exposes an explicit lifecycle whose legal transitions and terminal receipts remain stable across implementations.
pylons.name: Lifecycle refusal state machine
pylons.proof_transaction: Exercise every legal command, ambiguous command, reset, refusal, timeout, and fault path and prove terminal-state exclusivity plus state preservation.
pylons.shape_notation: discover -> configure -> load -> run -> read/capture, with reset/refuse/fault as explicit receipted transitions

pylons.authority_location: The receipt layer owns the alignment of state, entropy, environment, calibration, and time; the substrate supplies observations within that braid.
design_consequences: Classify determinism as exact, trace-replayable, or distributional.
Hash entropy and stochastic path traces when exact replay depends on them.
Bind calibration and environmental manifests to the execution interval.
Align events, power, clocks, and accepted output before comparison.
failure_modes: random seed substituted for physical entropy
calibration applied outside the measured interval
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse state, randomness, environment, calibration, and time into an opaque run identifier.
pylons.invariant: A result is replayable or statistically interpretable only when the causal custody of state, entropy, environment, calibration, and time is explicit.
pylons.name: Causal custody braid
pylons.proof_transaction: Replay an exact fixture with a retained trace, evaluate a distributional fixture without that trace, then shift calibration or clock alignment and require first-divergence refusal.
pylons.shape_notation: state + entropy/path + environment + calibration + synchronized time -> interpretable result

pylons.authority_location: The domain-level accepted semantics sit above every intermediate representation and target lowering; differential verification sits below each lowering edge.
design_consequences: Define the domain semantics before choosing target instructions or hardware.
Use a portable IR that retains state, path, precision, and timing assumptions.
Generate target-specific lowerings as replaceable commodities.
Differentially verify source, IR, target, and accepted output.
failure_modes: source location and information effects lost
backend success accepted without output parity
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse source semantics, portable representation, schedule, target encoding, and generated RTL into one compiler success event.
pylons.invariant: Semantics are preserved through an explicit sandwich of domain contract, portable IR, target lowering, and differential proof.
pylons.name: Semantic IR lowering sandwich
pylons.proof_transaction: Lower one accepted workload through two independent backends, compare source, IR, target traces, and accepted results, and emit first semantic divergence.
pylons.shape_notation: accepted semantics -> portable IR -> target lowering -> target execution, with differential proof across every edge

pylons.authority_location: Evidence tiers and measured replacement tests own fidelity; models and devices remain distinct witnesses.
design_consequences: Separate ideal, nonideal, calibrated, target-observed, measured, and independently validated tiers.
Name the model and solver at every tier.
Retain parameter, geometry, process, and uncertainty manifests.
Require measured behavior to replace rather than merely decorate simulation.
failure_modes: ideal model presented as device prediction
measurement used without model replacement map
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse ideal equations, compact models, simulation, calibration, target observation, and measurement into a single fidelity claim.
pylons.invariant: Physical confidence ascends a visible staircase whose transitions identify what new evidence replaced the prior abstraction.
pylons.name: Model-fidelity staircase
pylons.proof_transaction: Run a shared fixture through ideal, nonideal, calibrated, and measured tiers and record parameter identity plus first divergence at every transition.
pylons.shape_notation: ideal -> nonideal -> calibrated -> target-observed -> measured -> independently validated

pylons.authority_location: The held-out assay owns task separation and acceptance; sensing, substrate dynamics, readout, and training are independently receipted actors.
design_consequences: Compare raw stimulus, substrate response, and reference computation under one held-out split.
Receipt preprocessing, readout training, adaptation, sensing, and acquisition energy.
Require useful task gain beyond direct sensing.
Reject physical compute claims from interesting trajectories alone.
failure_modes: trajectory complexity mistaken for task gain
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse observation, transformation, readout, training, and accepted task performance into one substrate accuracy number.
pylons.invariant: A physical process earns compute credit only when its held-out response improves accepted task performance beyond raw sensing and a pinned comparison path.
pylons.name: Compute-versus-sensing separation
pylons.proof_transaction: Apply the same readout to raw input and substrate response on held-out episodes, include training and acquisition cost, and require positive compute gain before admission.
pylons.shape_notation: raw stimulus -> sensed input; substrate dynamics -> response; fixed readout -> held-out result; gain over raw decides compute

pylons.authority_location: The complete-system boundary owns cost attribution; primitives, hosts, links, converters, packages, sensors, and cooling are contributing components.
design_consequences: Declare every component required to deliver accepted work.
Include host, memory, interconnect, conversion, control, sensing, readout, package, and cooling.
Align all component costs to the same accepted-work interval.
Keep component and complete-system claims separate.
failure_modes: die metric promoted to system metric
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse a primitive, tile, die, card, package, rack, and facility into one denominator or boundary.
pylons.invariant: Useful work is judged inside the full envelope of components, transfers, conversions, controls, and environmental support required to produce it.
pylons.name: Complete-system envelope
pylons.proof_transaction: Expand one component result into a complete boundary, reconcile every energy and volume contribution, and compare the resulting accepted-work cost with the component-only report.
pylons.shape_notation: primitive inside host + memory + movement + conversion + control + sensing/readout + package + cooling = complete result envelope

pylons.authority_location: The accepted workload, matched baseline, complete boundary, and independent receipt own comparison. No provider chooses a scalar policy weight.
design_consequences: Report Energy, Volume, throughput, and latency as separate dimensions.
Require workload, boundary, environment, and claim scope to match the baseline.
Allow advantage only through Pareto dominance and complete measurement custody.
Keep ambient, signal-coupled, recovered, and external energy flows separate.
failure_modes: baseline uses different workload or boundary
component volume compared with rack performance
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse Energy, Volume, throughput, latency, workload quality, or measurement scope into a single self-authorizing score.
pylons.invariant: A candidate can claim complete-system advantage only when a matched, sealed baseline is no better on any EVP dimension and worse on at least one.
pylons.name: EVP Pareto frontier
pylons.proof_transaction: Measure candidate and baseline for identical accepted work, complete boundary, and environment, then emit separate EVP ratios and admit advantage only on Pareto dominance.
pylons.shape_notation: matched accepted work + complete boundary + sealed baseline -> E/V/throughput/latency vector -> Pareto admission

pylons.authority_location: The stable composition contract owns transport and lifecycle semantics; endpoints retain implementation freedom but no authority over the other endpoint.
design_consequences: Use stable versioned transport profiles and opaque handles.
Keep endpoint identity, state, reset, errors, and receipts explicit.
Account for coherency, protocol, retry, conversion, and package costs.
Permit link and endpoint replacement independently.
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse die, link, protocol, memory model, package, and endpoint lifecycle into one nominal bandwidth claim.
pylons.invariant: Composition occurs through a stable fabric contract that preserves endpoint replacement, opaque state custody, error behavior, and complete transfer receipts.
pylons.name: Composition fabric
pylons.proof_transaction: Run one accepted traffic and lifecycle fixture across two endpoint implementations and two transport profiles while preserving state, errors, reset, and transfer receipts.
pylons.shape_notation: replaceable endpoint A <-> stable fabric contract <-> replaceable endpoint B, with state/error/receipt custody

pylons.authority_location: The workload and complete-system receipt own the scale comparison; each scale boundary exposes its own communication, synchronization, refresh, and failure tax.
design_consequences: Model tile, die, package, board, rack, and facility boundaries separately.
Move communication and synchronization costs outward as the system scales.
Retain topology and utilization in the workload identity.
Require scale claims to reproduce accepted work rather than local link rate.
failure_modes: tile result multiplied into rack claim
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not extrapolate local device or link behavior across a scale seam without exposing the new communication and coordination mechanism.
pylons.invariant: Every increase in scale creates a new causal seam whose movement, synchronization, refresh, utilization, and failure costs must become explicit.
pylons.name: Scale-seam communication tax
pylons.proof_transaction: Execute the same accepted workload at two adjacent scales, preserve topology and utilization, and attribute the delta to communication, synchronization, refresh, and failure handling.
pylons.shape_notation: local compute + each new scale seam adds movement + synchronization + refresh + fault tax

pylons.authority_location: The signoff and measurement chain owns materialization evidence; compilers, PDKs, foundries, packages, and test services are replaceable stages.
design_consequences: Preserve source, model, RTL, netlist, layout, PDK, signoff, fabrication, package, and test identities.
Retain failed-run evidence and process deviations.
Require measured structures to map back to source and workload intent.
Maintain at least two viable materialization routes where possible.
failure_modes: GDS without source or PDK identity
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse generated RTL, signoff, fabrication, package, and measured silicon into one tape-out milestone.
pylons.invariant: A design becomes a physical candidate through a staged, replayable funnel whose every transformation and failed attempt remains attributable.
pylons.name: Materialization funnel
pylons.proof_transaction: Rebuild one source design through two tool or PDK routes, fabricate or emulate a test structure, and bind signoff plus measured output back to the same accepted artifact identity.
pylons.shape_notation: semantics/source -> generated implementation -> signoff -> fabrication -> package -> test -> measured receipt

pylons.authority_location: The submission package and returned raw artifacts remain under programme custody; the remote facility controls only the declared execution venue.
design_consequences: Package workload, configuration, expected output, fallback, and measurement requirements before submission.
Record queue, facility, hardware, firmware, and access identities.
Require raw returned artifacts and failed-run evidence.
Maintain an exit and migration route to another venue.
failure_modes: remote run represented only by dashboard result
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse a submission, queue, facility execution, returned summary, and independent acceptance into one remote-job identifier.
pylons.invariant: A remote venue is a replaceable execution envelope whose submission, queue, hardware, raw output, and exit conditions are separately receipted.
pylons.name: Remote venue envelope
pylons.proof_transaction: Submit one immutable package to two venues, reconstruct each run from returned raw artifacts, and migrate after intentional denial or venue removal without changing acceptance.
pylons.shape_notation: sealed submission -> queue/facility envelope -> raw returned artifacts -> local replay -> acceptance or migration

pylons.authority_location: The progress and energy trace receipts own recovery comparison; checkpoint, commit, reversible-history, retry, and cartridge strategies are peers.
design_consequences: Bind progress, commit state, failure schedule, and energy trace.
Compare checkpoint, task-atomic, reversible-history, retry, and substrate strategies under the same trace.
Account for lost work, storage, sensing, reset, and recovery energy.
Require the accepted result after every admissible interruption schedule.
failure_modes: checkpoint state lacks exact restoration semantics
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse completed work, retained progress, commit state, retries, and energy availability into one uptime percentage.
pylons.invariant: Recovery strategies are comparable only under identical work, failure, state, and energy traces with explicit lost-work and restoration receipts.
pylons.name: Intermittent commit and recovery
pylons.proof_transaction: Replay one accepted workload and failure schedule across checkpoint, task-atomic, reversible-history, retry, and cartridge execution, then compare retained progress and complete energy.
pylons.shape_notation: work + state + failure/energy trace -> commit/retry/reverse strategy -> restored accepted result + lost-work receipt

pylons.authority_location: The registry and completion programme own the map from public signal to system gap, first transaction, lane, and receipt. The external actor remains a source of commodity artifacts.
design_consequences: Pin every public source and reusable artifact before interpretation.
Map each actor to explicit system gaps rather than market categories alone.
Generate a bounded first transaction and required receipt for every record.
Preserve programme failure, access loss, and supersession as intake evidence.
pylons.forbidden_collapse: Do not collapse discovery, interpretation, dependency selection, execution, and qualification into an ecosystem recommendation.
pylons.invariant: Every public signal is converted into a pinned commodity record, named completion gap, bounded first transaction, execution lane, and required receipt.
pylons.name: Registry-gap transaction dispatch
pylons.proof_transaction: Remove an actor or programme from the registry, regenerate the completion plan, and prove that its system gaps and receipts remain covered by substitute records and lanes.
pylons.shape_notation: public signal -> pinned identity -> reusable asset + system gap -> first transaction -> lane -> receipt -> substitution
